evidence.summary: London's New Year's Eve display ran as planned on 31 December 2024 into 1 January 2025, with the Mayor's office reporting a completed fireworks and light show on the South Bank and no security incident.
evidence.rationale: The window he gave was explicit and narrow: darkness and something bad over England during the New Year countdown, told 10 November 2024 and repeated 17 November. The night passed without an attack, a mass casualty event or any incident of the kind he described.

evidence.summary: London Fire Brigade logged nearly 400 calls in the first two hours of 2025, attending a flat fire in Notting Hill, an outbuilding in Camden, a house in Forest Gate, several small firework fires and a road collision near Primrose Hill. None was treated as an attack.
evidence.rationale: This is the fullest incident record for the night and it is an ordinary busy New Year for a city of nine million. Base rate matters here: a handful of domestic fires and a road collision on the busiest night of the year is what London has every year, so nothing in it can be read back as the darkness he saw.

evidence.summary: UK Counter Terrorism Policing arrest data covering the period shows no attack or disrupted plot in England tied to 31 December 2024 or 1 January 2025; the significant British plot of the period, the Manchester synagogue case, was disrupted in 2025 and tried in December of that year.
evidence.rationale: Checked for a foiled plot as well as a completed attack, because his framing allows either to be claimed. Neither exists for that date in England. Worth recording alongside this: an attack did happen at the New Year, on Bourbon Street in New Orleans on 1 January 2025, but that belongs to the three named American cities he warned about, not to this England claim, and merging them would be reading the miss into the hit.
